thread:
Maria (Finance): Flagging an odd spike on Nexar's March bill — ~68k extra embed tokens between 02:58–03:05 UTC. Pattern looks like requests attributed to their org but with client_env="staging" and some with client_env="prod" in the same session. Could be a tagging issue. :thinking_face:
Tom (Infra): ack — thanks for the ping. I saw a couple of related alerts earlier about the tag-extraction lambda throwing ephemeral errors. Investigating now. :eyes:
Tom (Infra): quick query I ran: ```SELECT client_org, client_env, COUNT(*) AS calls, SUM(tokens) AS tokens FROM metering.calls WHERE client_org='nexar' AND ts >= '2026-03-12T02:55:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-03-12T03:10:00Z' GROUP BY client_org, client_env;``` Result: prod=1.2k calls / 12k tokens, staging=6.8k calls / 68k tokens. staging traffic unusually high under nexar org id.
Jen (Billing): If staging was mis-labeled as nexar-prod we should not bill them for internal staging runs. Can we confirm these requests originated from our internal staging pool or from nexar's staging infra?
Tom (Infra): Tracing request headers — many have X-Env: staging but originate from the same IP ranges as other Nexar prod traffic; however the auth token issuer field looks like our internal deploy tokens (deploy-infra-**). That suggests our staging harness accidentally used Nexar API keys in a test job or our tagging function used the wrong header.
Aisha (Customer Success): I'm looping in Nexar's engineer (cc: @nexar-eng) to confirm they're not intentionally hitting prod. They replied earlier today that they were running a large load test on staging. They deny sharing prod keys. Could be our test runner used a copied API key.
Maria (Finance): OK action items: 1) Pause invoicing for Nexar's March bill window and mark the 68k tokens as disputed. 2) Infra to identify root cause and provide exact request ids for backfill. 3) Billing to prepare a credit if the tokens are internal/test. We should also block auto-collection until resolved.
Jen (Billing): I'm putting a temporary credit hold on invoice INV-2026-03-NEXAR and flagging the account so no automated payments run. Created ticket BILL-9123.
billing-bot: Billing hold placed: invoice INV-2026-03-NEXAR paused by Jen. Reason: disputed usage spike (possible internal staging traffic).
Tom (Infra): Root cause appears to be a race where the tag-extractor lambda fell back to a cached header mapping when the org header was missing, and the cache keyer used the previous request's org id. Patch ready: avoid cross-request cache reuse and add a hard check for token issuer. Deploying now to canary. Diff: `fix/tag-cache-scope`
Aisha (Customer Success): Nexar confirmed they found one of our internal test jobs had a copy of their API key in a CI config (accidental leak on their side). They're going to rotate keys immediately but want a credit for the runs.
Maria (Finance): Given that both infra and Nexar agree the traffic was testing/staging, we'll credit Nexar for the 68,000 embed tokens and re-run metering backfill after the fix. Please include the list of request ids and a checksum of the corrected usage.
Tom (Infra): I'll export request ids and raw events to a secure bucket and share the s3 link in the backfill ticket. ETA 2 hours for export, then backfill job.
Jen (Billing): Once backfill completes, we'll issue a pro-rated credit on the current invoice and add a note to the account explaining the credit reason. I'll draft the customer-facing message for Aisha to review.
Aisha (Customer Success): Thanks — please cc me on the message. I'll coordinate key rotation confirmation from Nexar and confirm they accept the credit.
Maria (Finance): Thanks team. Follow-ups: BILL-9123 (billing hold + credit), INFRA-4831 (fix deployed + export), METER-2207 (backfill run). I'll close this thread when credit posts and invoice amount updates. :white_check_mark:
